title: About
text:
My name is Thomas Scherer. I have worked in government at the US Institute of Peace, academia at the University of California, San Diego, non-profits at the think tank fp21, and media at Bloomberg Economics. I am a volunteer firefighter, gamer, and husky dad. I earned a PhD in international relations from Princeton University.
I am the author of AbroadReview, a living literature review on topics in foreign policy and international relations (also available on Beehiiv and Substack). It’s goal is to provide a clear perspective on world events based on theories and evidence from international relations academic research.
AI usage: No AI is used in any writing on this website, just Grammarly. I have used Gemini to assist with coding in Quarto and R for creating the website.

About the website
This website is built on Quarto and hosted on Github. It was widely adapted from a template by Dr. Gang He.

title: Accountability in U.S. Foreign Policy
text:
This post is a placeholder for a future project.
There seems to be a lack of accountability in U.S. foreign policy. Was anyone held responsible for the 2003 invasion of Iraq?
Professions develop accountability mechanisms all the time. Doctors have to maintain their license. Lawyers can be disbarred. Why isn’t there something similar in foreign policy? It may be helpful to distinguish between politicians, foreign service, and ‘thought leaders’.
Is there anything to be learned from other countries? There are many examples of other democracies holding leaders accountable for their actions, but are any of them due to foreign policy?
